title: Applicability of Mortgage Insurance and the Loan-to-Value Basis on Home Mortgage Loans
content:
Private mortgage insurance applies on a Home Mortgage Loans note only on programs that carry an attachment loan-to-value figure, and then only where the original loan-to-value of that loan exceeded it.

## The loan-to-value the insurance rules are read against

The loan-to-value is measured on the original property value, and never on a new appraisal. On any measurement date it is the principal balance divided by the original property value, expressed as a percent to two decimals.

## Effect of removing insurance

Where insurance is removed from a loan, the monthly escrow deposit falls by the premium that had been included in it, from the next installment onward.

## Worked figures on hypothetical inputs

A loan was made at an original property value of $300000.00.

- With a principal balance of $240000.00 on the measurement date, the loan-to-value is 80.00 percent.
- With a principal balance of $237500.00, the loan-to-value is 79.17 percent to two decimals.
- With a principal balance of $234000.00, the loan-to-value is 78.00 percent.

Each of these is taken against the $300000.00 original property value. A later appraisal putting the property at $340000.00 does not enter the measurement, and the loan-to-value on a balance of $240000.00 remains 80.00 percent.

## Points of judgement

The attachment figure is a boundary of exceeding: insurance applies where the original loan-to-value exceeded the program's figure. A program that carries no attachment figure carries no private mortgage insurance on this basis at all.
